facts.text: I'm here to check on my blood pressure, because I've been diagnosed with hypertension.

facts.item: high blood pressure: when it was found
facts.text: I discovered I had high blood pressure last year.

facts.item: high blood pressure: control on treatment
facts.text: Even with the hydrochlorothiazide, my blood pressure is still elevated.

facts.item: high blood pressure: checking it at home
facts.text: I don't check my blood pressure at home.
It was last checked six months ago.
I feel fine.
I've started to have problems with my sexual performance.
It started over the past 4 months.
I have a weak erection.

facts.item: problems with sexual performance: unable to get an erection
facts.text: Sometimes I can't get an erection at all.

facts.item: problems with sexual performance: erection strength score
facts.text: About a 4, where 0 is flaccid and 6 is enough for penetration.

facts.item: problems with sexual performance: own explanation
facts.text: A friend told me it's the propranolol, but I think it's my age.
I don't have early morning or night-time erections.
My sex drive has diminished, Doc. I'm not as interested in sex as I used to be.
I've been losing more hair than usual from my head.
I think I'm starting to go bald.
There haven't been any changes in my mood.
I've been happy, other than my concern about not being able to perform.
I'm not anxious.
I'm not stressed.
I don't have any pain when walking or resting.
My weight hasn't changed.
My appetite hasn't changed.
I was diagnosed with high cholesterol last year.
I've never been diagnosed with diabetes.
My sugar levels were tested six months ago.
I haven't had any heart problems.
I haven't had a stroke.
I've never had a mini-stroke.
I haven't had any other diagnoses besides the blood pressure and the cholesterol.
I haven't had any trauma.
I haven't had any surgery.
I don't have any drug allergies.
I was prescribed hydrochlorothiazide for my blood pressure.
Six months ago, propranolol was added for my blood pressure.
In general, I take my medications regularly.

facts.item: taking the medications as prescribed: missed doses
facts.text: Well, sometimes I forget to take the pills.
I take lovastatin for my cholesterol.
My father died of a heart attack at the age of 50.
My mother is healthy, but she has Alzheimer's disease.
My mother is in a nursing home now.
I eat a lot of junk food.
I don't exercise.
I drink beer.
Three to four beers a week.
I've been drinking like that for the last decade.
I don't use any illegal drugs.
I don't smoke.
Before these problems, I was intimate a few times each week with my wife.
My family life is the same as it has always been.
I am very happy in my job.
I'm a schoolteacher.
My wife and I live together in our home.

evidence: Onset of erectile dysfunction coincides with propranolol use

differential.diagnosis: Erectile dysfunction secondary to vascular disease

other_considerations.note: Psychogenic causes reduce libido and erections but usually spare nocturnal or morning erections, which are absent here; he denies other depressive symptoms, though his feelings about his mother in a nursing home may deserve exploration.
Fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea can cause penile scarring and erectile dysfunction.

x001: The note says 'VS: within normal limits', but the doorway BP of 135/88 mm Hg is above the 130/80 target named in the sample closure.
x016: Faithful to the source, but clinically implausible next to an otherwise normal neurological exam; likely a source error. Direction of the plantar response is not stated. Review before use.

leakage.reason: A friend's attribution of the sexual problems to propranolol points directly at the rank-1 diagnosis (medication-induced erectile dysfunction); it is scripted history the SP gives, so it is kept.

source_issues: Age conflict: the opening scenario says 50 years old; the raw Patient Description and the note HPI say 54. demographics.age uses the opening scenario (50).

Exam line e009 says 'bilateral Babinski sign present'. Read literally this is an abnormal (upgoing) plantar response, which fits poorly with an otherwise normal lower-extremity neuro exam and is not mentioned in the gold; it is kept neutral in x016 (direction not stated).
The note says 'VS: within normal limits' (e002), but the doorway BP is 135/88 mm Hg, above the 130/80 target named in the sample closure.
The raw Patient Description says the patient 'appears anxious', but he denies anxiety and stress (p016).
p002 'my blood pressure is still elevated' is ambiguous in time (before or after propranolol was added); temporality unclear, so f003 has no time.
Note PSH reads 'No, I do not.' (script wording copied into the note).
Gold rank 1 'Onset of erectile dysfunction coincides with propranolol use': propranolol was added 6 months ago and the problems began 4 months ago; roughly consistent.
The challenging question has a doubled opening quotation mark in the source; cleaned.
notes: The visit is a hypertension follow-up, so hypertension course facts (diagnosis, persistent elevation, home monitoring, last check) are symptom facts (v1 hpi), as children of the visit-reason fact f001; the drugs are medication facts.
p020 is split into never diagnosed with diabetes (f025) and last blood-sugar test six months ago with no result given (f026).
Note-only facts (v1 from_note): no TIA (f029) and no history of trauma (f031).
The scripted 'Isn't that right, doctor?' in p008 is in extras.patient_questions next to the challenging question.
leakage lists f012 because it names propranolol as the cause, which is the rank-1 diagnosis.
14 template answers (No, I do not.) checked against the June-2024 release: all are plain denials there; 15 facts confirmed (flags re-keyed to the v2 ids).

The own explanations of the sexual problems (f012) and the hair loss (f016) are v1 'concerns', so they keep category social_background although their parents are symptoms; their system is omitted because they are not symptom facts.
